title: The outbreak
paradigm: Tversky & Kahneman (1981) Asian disease problem, between-subjects framing
intro: Imagine a country is preparing for the outbreak of an unusual disease that is expected to kill 600 people. Two alternative programmes have been proposed. Which would you choose?

options.text: Programme A: 200 people will be saved.
Programme B: there is a 1/3 chance that 600 people will be saved, and a 2/3 chance that no one will be saved.
Programme D: there is a 1/3 chance that nobody will die, and a 2/3 chance that 600 people will die.

debrief: Programmes A and C are identical (200 live, 400 die), and so are B and D. In the original study 72% chose the sure option when it was framed as lives saved, but 78% chose the gamble when it was framed as deaths. You saw only one frame; the other frame is shown here so you can check whether your choice would have flipped.
